brief.headline: Memory pair trade inconclusive; HBM4 transition accelerating but Q3 pricing signals buyer fatigue
brief.summary: <cite index="40-11,40-13">Samsung and SK Hynix erased billions mid-session July 2, falling 7-14% as Nasdaq tech selloff spread to Korea</cite>, though <cite index="44-3">Kospi rebounded 5.8% on July 3 with Samsung +8.2% and SK Hynix +10.9%</cite>. <cite index="10-1">TrendForce projects conventional DRAM prices +13-18% QoQ in Q3 2026 and NAND +10-15%, slowing from Q1's record 93-98% DRAM surge</cite>, while <cite index="16-1,16-14">ADATA warned DRAM contract prices will rise 20-30% and NAND 35-40% in Q3</cite>. <cite index="7-7,7-8">Samsung began HBM4 mass production in February 2026 at 11.7Gbps with 40% power efficiency gains, marking industry-first commercial shipments</cite>, but <cite index="4-17">UBS forecasts SK Hynix will capture ~70% of HBM4 market share for Nvidia Rubin in 2026</cite>. <cite index="25-5,25-7">Hyperscalers plan $725B capex in 2026—Amazon $200B, Google $185B, Meta $125B, Microsoft $120B—up 77% from $410B in 2025</cite>, sustaining HBM demand despite <cite index="13-26">buyers no longer chasing higher spot quotes and NAND spot trading gone quiet</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="4-17">SK Hynix expected to secure ~70% HBM4 market share for Nvidia Rubin platform in 2026 per UBS</cite>, extending its <cite index="4-10,4-11">Q2 2025 HBM shipment share of 62% and Q3 revenue share of 57%</cite>. <cite index="7-7,7-10">Samsung shipped first commercial HBM4 in February 2026 and anticipates HBM sales to triple vs 2025</cite>, with <cite index="2-20,2-21">favorable feedback in Nvidia HBM4 SiP tests while SK Hynix already supplies paid HBM4 samples</cite>. Near-term edge to SK Hynix on qualification timing and Nvidia allocation; Samsung closing gap on HBM4E and 16-layer roadmap, but ADR volatility (SKHY <cite index="43-1">whipsawed 27% surge to 5% drop</cite>) and <cite index="46-7,46-12">bear-market technicals—both down >20% from recent highs, Micron off $350B</cite>—neutralize tactical calls. Watch Samsung HBM4 qual announcements and SK Hynix <cite index="40-14,40-15">M17 NAND fab (100 trillion won, operations H1 2029) and P&T7 packaging (20 trillion won)</cite> for capacity differentiation.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="13-1,13-10">Q1 2026 conventional DRAM prices rose 93-98% QoQ, buyers paid roughly double three months earlier</cite>; <cite index="14-2,14-7">Q2 DRAM +58-63% QoQ, NAND +70-75% QoQ per TrendForce</cite>. <cite index="10-1">Q3 DRAM forecast decelerated to +13-18% QoQ, NAND +10-15%</cite>. <cite index="17-3,17-9">Q1 saw 90-95% DRAM QoQ and LPDDR5x ~90% QoQ, NAND +55-60% QoQ</cite>. <cite index="13-16,13-17">Samsung/SK Hynix weighed 20-30% NAND price hikes; TrendForce expects new NAND supply not until late 2027 or 2028</cite>. <cite index="13-21,13-24">HBM consumes wafer capacity that would produce commodity DRAM; through Q2 memory prices rising across the board, NAND leading on contract, spot DDR4/DDR5 ticking up into early June</cite>. <cite index="13-25,13-26">First strain sign: buyers no longer chasing higher spot quotes, NAND spot trading gone quiet</cite>. Structural: <cite index="15-21,15-22">AI demand permanently raised baseline consumption; hyperscaler capex among top eight CSPs projected to exceed $600B in 2026, +40% YoY</cite>.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="4-7,4-9">HBM3E expected to remain flagship product in 2026, accounting for ~two-thirds of total HBM shipments</cite>, while <cite index="6-13">2026 HBM revenue mix forecast at ~55% HBM4, 45% HBM3E with HBM4 ramping Q3</cite>. <cite index="2-11,2-13">Nvidia recently asked suppliers for 16-layer HBM delivery Q4 2026; performance evaluation expected before Q3</cite>, <cite index="2-16">16-layer likely classified HBM4, naming could shift to HBM4E</cite>. <cite index="7-1,7-2">Samsung HBM4 offers 2.7x bandwidth vs HBM3E (max 3.3 TB/s per stack), 24-36GB capacity via 12-layer stacking</cite>; <cite index="3-3,3-5">SK Hynix HBM4 doubles I/O to 2,048 terminals, >40% power efficiency gain, >10Gbps speed vs 8Gbps JEDEC standard</cite>. <cite index="8-4">HBM3 ~$200/stack, HBM3E ~$300/stack, HBM4 ~$500/stack (July 2026 estimates)</cite>. <cite index="6-2,6-4">Samsung/SK Hynix prioritizing HBM4 ramp keeps HBM3E supply tight; HBM3E demand exceeded expectations following H200 export approval to China, launches by Google TPU and Amazon Trainium</cite>. <cite index="6-9,6-10">HBM content per accelerator +20-30% vs earlier generations; Google TPU v7 integrates eight HBM3E stacks, Amazon Trainium3 uses four</cite>. Packaging bottleneck easing: <cite index="30-10">CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from ~20% to ~10% by end-2026</cite>, <cite index="34-1,34-3">TSMC CoWoS capacity 115-140k wpm end-2026, ~170k wpm 2027</cite>.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung ships industry-first commercial HBM4, anticipates 3x HBM sales growth in 2026
news_pulse.implication: Samsung closed qual gap with February 2026 HBM4 launch at 11.7Gbps; HBM4E sampling H2 2026, custom HBM 2027. Upside to HBM revenue guidance if Nvidia/hyperscaler adoption accelerates.

news_pulse.headline: Nvidia requests 16-layer HBM delivery by Q4 2026, pulling forward generational transition
news_pulse.implication: Nvidia testing supplier capacity for 16-layer HBM (HBM4/HBM4E) before 12-layer HBM4 reaches full rollout. Samsung focusing hybrid bonding for 16-layer; SK Hynix maximizing MR-MUF. Q4 qual results critical for 2027 allocation.

news_pulse.headline: TrendForce: Q3 2026 DRAM price growth decelerates to +13-18% QoQ, NAND +10-15% QoQ
news_pulse.implication: Deceleration from Q1's 93-98% DRAM surge signals affordability ceiling hit; server DRAM protected by long-term contracts, consumer demand softening. Pricing power intact through Q3 but rate-of-change rolling over.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler capex hits $725B in 2026, up 77% YoY led by Amazon $200B, Google $185B
news_pulse.implication: AI infrastructure spend sustains HBM/server DRAM demand despite capex-to-revenue gap widening to 46% per Allianz, exceeding 2001 telecom divergence of 32%. ROI scrutiny rising but no pullback visible.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrows to ~10% by end-2026 from ~20% currently
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS capacity expansion to 115-140k wpm end-2026, 170k wpm 2027 eases HBM packaging bottleneck. Nvidia B200/GB200 and AMD MI400 supply constraints moderating; orders spilling to Intel/ASE/Amkor.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix invests 100 trillion won: M17 NAND fab (80T, ops H1 2029), P&T7 packaging (20T)
news_pulse.implication: M17 targets enterprise SSD/NAND for AI; P&T7 expands advanced packaging. Construction 2027, operations 2029—no near-term supply relief but signals confidence in AI storage demand durability.

news_pulse.headline: Memory stocks enter bear market: Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron down >20% from recent highs
news_pulse.implication: Semiconductor basket lost ~$1.5T market cap since June 25; Micron off $350B. Samsung Q2 profit beat failed to impress. Technicals deteriorating despite structural HBM tailwinds—profit-taking or demand concern?

news_pulse.headline: ADATA warns Q3 2026 DRAM prices +20-30%, NAND +35-40%; shortages to 2028
news_pulse.implication: Module maker passing through supplier price hikes; NAND outpacing DRAM in Q3. AI capacity crowding out consumer supply. Q4 2026 seen +40-50% sequentially if AI consumption persists.

brief.derivatives_signal: <cite index="43-7,43-8">SKHY put/call ratio 1.12 across full chain, Micron 0.91</cite>; <cite index="43-1,43-12">SK Hynix ADR whipsawed 27% surge to 5% drop, thin float and ADR premium to Seoul shares driving volatility</cite>. <cite index="40-3">SK Hynix ADR began Nasdaq trading July 10</cite>; <cite index="44-2">single-stock leveraged ETFs linked to Samsung/SK Hynix plummeted below 20,000 won listing price July 15</cite>. <cite index="43-3">Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) holds Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron each 24%</cite>—proxy for memory exposure but high vol. <cite index="46-1,46-7">All four down >20% from closing highs, bear-market threshold</cite>. Options skew defensive but July volatility unrelated to fundamentals; watch SKHY ADR premium/discount to 000660.KS for arb flows and retail leveraged ETF liquidations for forced selling.
